observations: All five strategies matched an independently fresh-rebuilt exact rank vector at every one of the 1083 effective boundary updates.
periodic_32 reduced maximum allocated/live ratio in all 12 cells and maximum current allocated nodes in all 12 cells versus always_incremental.

periodic_32 had lower strategy runtime in 9/12 cells and 5.54% lower summed strategy time in this Python run; timing is descriptive and may reflect reduced stale-node/cache pressure rather than a general runtime guarantee.

ratio_4 and hybrid_ratio4_or_64 rebuilt 532 times and were identical in this matrix because fresh managers themselves frequently had allocation/live ratio >=4; the threshold therefore behaved nearly like always_rebuild rather than a selective trigger.
always_rebuild used 1083 rebuilds and substantially more cumulative allocations; periodic_32 used 30 rebuilds.
scope: New small V1 holdout only (n=10,12,14). V0 larger-size preregistration remains incomplete due runtime timeout and is not inferred from V1. Cell-level execution data are summarized rather than reproduced in full here; exact aggregate evidence is from the preregistered run in the current Python environment.
